notes: Summary: SpectraIDE builds an enterprise-grade IDE copilot used by ~600 developers across multiple product teams. Primary ask: dedicated capacity to guarantee <40ms token latency under interactive typing workloads and deterministic throughput during 10:00-16:00 PST peak. Want low-latency streaming (server->client chunked responses), model/version pinning per workspace, and graceful fallback to smaller quantized variants if capacity constrained. Key quotes: "We need typing latency — not batch latency — to feel instantaneous for developers." Security: must support SSO (SAML), audit logs for token-level access, KMS for key control, and EU data residency for EU teams. Economics: highly cost-sensitive on sustained tokens but OK to pay for reserved baseline + burst credits. POC notes: current open model baseline shows latency spikes at concurrent editor sessions >600; request: 1 dedicated GPU pool for peak hours with autoscale buffer + burst policy to handle 900 concurrent sessions. SE actions: run deterministic load test (script attached in drive), propose quantization profile (int8) for code-gen models, and provide estimated cost curves (reserved vs spot/burst). Sales notes: target ARR $120k first year, expansion to $400k next 24 months if dedicated pool meets SLOs. Next steps: 48-hour dedicated POC scheduled, legal to review DPA, finance to approve forecast cap. Staccato CRM style: emailed pricing deck 2026-02-20; awaiting signed NDA. Phone call snippets: "If we can keep median latency <25ms typing tokens we're happy" — noted by VP Eng. Follow-ups: schedule post-POC wrap on 2026-03-05 and decision by end of April.
short_description: Enterprise IDE copilot vendor evaluating Redwood Dedicated for guaranteed low-latency interactive code generation and predictable peak throughput.
